references.text: Amos uses Jacob's historical weakness ('so small') as a theological image of Israel's dependence on God's grace, paralleling Jacob's own concern in Gen 33.
The same theological motif as candidate 2: 'Jacob is small' as an image of vulnerability that requires God's intervention.
Clear contrast: Zechariah describes scattering at the shepherd's fall, while Jacob in Gen 33 struggles to keep the flock together.
Jacob appears as a responsible shepherd who protects the weak, in contrast to Ezekiel's criticism of irresponsible shepherds.
